parameters.content:
### 1. Start

**You press Execute.**

Nothing here runs on a schedule or a trigger. The workflow does nothing until you click the button yourself.

assignments.name: classifyPrompt
assignments.value:
You are a precise sentiment analyst for YouTube comments.
You receive a JSON array of comments, each with an "id" and "text".

For EVERY comment decide:
- sentiment: "positive" | "negative" | "neutral"
  positive = praise, gratitude, enjoyment, agreement, enthusiasm, affection
  negative = criticism, complaint, disappointment, disagreement, hostility
  neutral  = questions, factual statements, timestamps, greetings, off-topic
             chatter, self-promotion, or genuinely ambiguous text
- aspects: 0 to 2 short lowercase noun phrases (1-3 words) naming WHAT the
  comment is about - e.g. "audio quality", "editing", "host energy",
  "video length", "background music", "explanation clarity", "thumbnail",
  "ads", "camera work", "pacing". Only include an aspect when the comment
  actually names or clearly implies one; otherwise use [].
  Reuse identical wording for the same concept across comments.

Rules:
- Judge sarcasm and irony by intent, not by literal wording.
- Comments may be in any language; read them in that language but always
  output aspect labels in English.
- Emoji-only comments: judge by the emoji.
- Praise for the creator or channel counts as positive even when it does not
  name a specific aspect.
- Return exactly one entry per input id. Never omit, merge or invent ids.

Respond with JSON only, in this exact shape:
{"results":[{"id":0,"sentiment":"positive","aspects":["editing"]}]}

assignments.name: summaryPrompt
assignments.value:
You are summarising sentiment analysis of the comments on one YouTube video.

You will receive: the video metadata, aggregate sentiment counts, raw aspect
tags with frequencies, and the most-liked example comments per sentiment.

The raw aspect tags contain duplicates and near-synonyms ("audio", "audio
quality", "sound") - MERGE synonyms into one canonical aspect and SUM their
counts. Never invent a count: every number you output must be a sum of the
counts you were given.

Ground every claim in the aspects and example comments provided. Where the
evidence is thin, say so plainly rather than padding. Do not praise or
flatter the creator; describe what the audience actually said.

Respond with JSON only, in this exact shape:
{
  "overall": "2-3 sentences on how the audience received this video",
  "positive_summary": "3-5 sentences on what viewers praised",
  "negative_summary": "3-5 sentences on what viewers criticised",
  "neutral_summary": "2-3 sentences on what the neutral comments consist of",
  "top_positive_aspects": [{"aspect":"Audio Quality","count":42}],
  "top_negative_aspects": [{"aspect":"Video Length","count":17}],
  "requests": ["concrete things viewers asked for"],
  "recommendations": ["actionable suggestions for the creator"]
}

Aspect labels: Title Case, 1-4 words. Max 8 aspects per list, sorted by count
descending. Max 5 requests and 5 recommendations. Use an empty array when
there is nothing to report.

### 2. Settings

**Every dial, in one place.**

Paste your video link into `videoUrl`. This is also where you change the AI models, rewrite the prompts, set how many comments to pull, and pick the report colours — all without opening any code.

### 3. Extract Video ID

**Reads the link you pasted.**

Pulls the 11-character video ID out of it. Understands normal watch links, youtu.be short links, Shorts, live streams, and a bare ID typed on its own.

nodes.name: Extract Video ID — what this does

parameters.content:
### 4. Get Video Info

**Asks YouTube about the video itself.**

Title, channel name, thumbnail, view count, like count. These fill in the header of your report so you know which video it describes.

_Needs the YouTube credential._

nodes.name: Get Video Info — what this does

parameters.content:
### 5. Fetch Comments

**Downloads the comments.**

YouTube only hands over 100 at a time, so this keeps asking for the next page until it runs out or hits your `maxPages` limit (20 pages = 2,000 comments).

Top-level comments only — replies are skipped.

### 6. Clean & Batch

**Tidies the pile up.**

Strips HTML out of the comment text, drops duplicates and copy-paste spam, then splits what is left into stacks of 80.

The AI reads one stack at a time instead of all 2,000 comments at once.

### 7. Classify Sentiment

**The AI reads every comment.**

Each stack goes to the model, which marks every comment positive, negative or neutral and tags what it is about ("audio quality", "too long").

Many small calls, not one huge one: cheaper, more accurate, and if one stack fails the run carries on without it.

_Needs the OpenRouter credential._

### 8. Aggregate Results

**Adds it all up.**

How many positive, negative and neutral. Which topics came up most often, split by whether people were praising or complaining. And which comments got the most likes — those become the quotes in your report.

### 9. Generate Summaries

**One last AI call, for the writing.**

It reads the totals, not the raw comments. It merges topic labels that mean the same thing ("audio" and "sound" become one), then writes the plain-English summaries of what people liked and disliked.

### 10. Build Dashboard

**Draws the report.**

Turns the numbers into a web page: the sentiment bar, the stat boxes, the two topic charts, the summaries and the example comments.

Layout and styling live in this node's code.

### 11. Create HTML File

**Saves it as a file you can open.**

Run the workflow, then click the download icon in this node's output panel. The file opens in any browser and can be emailed or shared as-is.

nodes.name: Create HTML File — what this does

parameters.content:
## YouTube comment sentiment analysis

Paste a video link, get a report: how many comments were positive, negative or neutral, what people praised, what they complained about, and the quotes that back it up.

### Set this up once, before the first run

**1.** Create a **Query Auth** credential named `YouTube API Key` — Name: `key`, Value: your YouTube Data API v3 key.
Select it on *Get Video Info* and *Fetch Comments*.

**2.** Create a **Header Auth** credential named `OpenRouter` — Name: `Authorization`, Value: `Bearer sk-or-v1-…`
Select it on *Classify Sentiment* and *Generate Summaries*.

**3.** Open **Settings**, paste your link into `videoUrl`, press Execute.

_A 2,000-comment run takes a few minutes and costs a few cents. Start with `maxPages` at 5 to try it out._

### Before you change the colours

The defaults were checked with a colourblind-safety validator.

Red/green is the obvious choice for sentiment and the wrong one — the two are hard to tell apart for roughly 8% of viewers. Blue ↔ red passes in both light and dark mode.

Change them if you want; just know what the trade is.
